rubric: One element is clearly read first: the headline is much larger than the body text and nothing else competes with it.
There is exactly one primary call to action; the secondary link is visibly quieter than the button.
The paragraph under the headline has a comfortable line length (about 40 to 75 characters) and secondary text still has strong contrast against its background.
Spacing groups the headline, paragraph and buttons as one unit, with generous whitespace and consistent alignment of edges.
The product visual looks specific to an invoice-reminder tool and supports the message without competing with the headline.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A looks more like a finished startup site: it has a brand mark, a clear two-line headline with an accent word, and a tilted invoice card with an 'Unpaid' tag and 'Reminder sent' status that fits the product. Its floating badges run to the very edge of the screen, and the 'Unpaid' tag crowds the invoice number, but these are small flaws. B has no logo, and its overlapping cards hide the second invoice's number and amount ('00.00'), which looks broken. B's trust line also wraps awkwardly and weakens the grouping. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B feels more like a real startup site. It has a brand mark, a clear headline with a gradient accent, a well-measured paragraph, and an invoice card that tells the reminder story well, though the UNPAID badge crowds the invoice number and the floating badges sit tight against the right edge. A has a solid hierarchy and calm spacing, but it has no brand. Its overlapping cards also hide the second invoice's number and amount, and the trust line below the buttons wraps awkwardly.
